contracts: Every public name (SPLUNK_INDEX, INVESTIGATOR_MAX_ITER, LLM_MODEL, AUTH_JSON_PATH, etc.) is a flat module-level constant assigned from one _settings = _Settings() instance at import time — consumers use `from splunk.config import X` or `config.X` exactly as before the pydantic-settings migration; nothing reaches through a nested settings object.

Direct runtime mutation of a public name (`config.SPLUNK_URL = url`, done by splunk/tui.py's Config screen on save) is a supported pattern — it reassigns the flat module attribute and is independent of the underlying _Settings instance.

Static defaults with no env var (CERT_FIELDS, CERT_ANOMALY_KEYWORDS, CORRELATE_PAIR_PATTERNS, DURATION_FIELDS, STATUS_CODE_FIELDS, ANOMALY_NUMERIC_FIELDS) stay plain module constants outside the _Settings class — not forced into pydantic fields just for consistency.
auth.py/client.py/agent.py no longer call load_dotenv() themselves (removed — was redundant once config.py loads .env on its own and none of those modules read os.environ directly for anything else).
config-settings.description: Centralised configuration, backed by a pydantic-settings BaseSettings class (_Settings, env_file=".env") so .env is loaded automatically regardless of import order — replaces a prior design where config.py read os.environ directly with no load_dotenv() of its own, silently ignoring .env unless some other already-imported module (auth.py/client.py/agent.py) happened to call load_dotenv() first.
invariants: config.py is the only place .env is read for config purposes; do not add load_dotenv() calls to other modules to work around a var not appearing — add it as a _Settings field instead.
SPLUNK_ prefix env var names match the _Settings field names 1:1 (case-sensitive) — pydantic-settings' default env var matching, no aliasing needed.
config-settings.name: config-settings

contracts: LLMBackend.check_available() fails fast with a clear message if the backend can't be used right now (missing binary, Ollama not running, model not pulled).

LLMBackend.bind_tools(tools) returns an object with .invoke(messages) -> AIMessage (with .tool_calls when the model wants to call a tool) -- this is the shape agent_node's ReAct loop requires, and it must be called exactly once per analyse() invocation then reused across every ReAct iteration (see agent.py's _build_graph/_make_agent_node), not once per iteration -- CLI backends rely on that single bound object surviving the whole loop to keep one --resume session alive instead of minting a fresh CLI session every turn.
get_backend(name, model) is the only public factory; unknown names raise ValueError listing valid choices.

For claude_cli/copilot_cli, tool schemas are described in the system prompt and the model is asked to reply with {"tool": name, "args": {...}} or {"final_answer": ...} -- _CLIToolCallingModel parses that JSON and translates it into a LangChain-shaped AIMessage so agent.py's graph doesn't need to know which backend is active.
llm-backend-seam.description: Pluggable chat-backend abstraction for splunk/agent.py's LangGraph ReAct loop, selected via config.AGENT_BACKEND (SPLUNK_AGENT_BACKEND env var). Three backends: 'ollama' (native LangChain tool-calling via ChatOllama), 'claude_cli' and 'copilot_cli' (shell to `claude -p`/`copilot -p` non-interactively with the CLI's own tool use disabled, bridging tool-calling by hand via a JSON protocol -- see splunk/cli_tool_protocol.py).
invariants: Session state (self._session_id, self._sent_message_signatures on _CLIToolCallingModel) is scoped to one analyse() call and discarded after -- unlike bee-bug-hunter's disk-persisted multi-role session store, agent.py has a single role and analyse() is one-shot per investigation, so no cross-process persistence or session forking is needed here.

Claude CLI supports --append-system-prompt (system and user text sent separately); Copilot CLI does not and folds both into one combined -p argument -- this asymmetry is handled per-backend in llm_backends.py, not in the shared cli_tool_protocol.py.
llm-backend-seam.name: llm-backend-seam

contracts: analyse(findings: dict) -> tuple[str, list[str]] is the sole public entry point; its return shape is a contract consumed by connector.py at two call sites and must not change without updating both.

Domain-specific investigation guidance (prompts + SPL query templates) lives in splunk/investigation_areas.INVESTIGATION_AREAS, not hardcoded in agent.py's tool bodies — request_deeper_analysis and generate_followup_queries both read from it via get_prompt/get_spl_template.

LogAnalysisState.hypotheses tracks root-cause candidates registered via rank_hypotheses (status starts 'open'); format_report's confirmed_hypothesis arg marks one confirmed and all other open ones rejected. This state is internal to a single analyse() graph invocation only — it does not persist across the outer per-iteration analyse() calls in connector.py's investigation loop.

Tool call arguments (not tool return strings) are the channel for state mutation in tool_node_fn — it reads args from the preceding AIMessage.tool_calls, matched by tool_call_id, rather than parsing sentinel markers out of a tool's return value (format_report's return value is used verbatim as the final report, so it must stay clean).
standalone-agent-langgraph.description: LangGraph ReAct agent (Qwen2.5 via Ollama) used only behind the --investigate CLI flag / connector.py's run_standalone_agent path — the fallback investigation loop for environments without Copilot/Claude driving MCP directly. Reasons over detector findings via a small tool set and emits a markdown report through format_report.
invariants: should_continue ends the loop when iterations >= AGENT_MAX_ITER OR when all tracked hypotheses are resolved (non-'open'), whichever comes first.
Adding a new investigation domain requires only a new entry in INVESTIGATION_AREAS, not edits to agent.py's tool logic.
standalone-agent-langgraph.name: standalone-agent-langgraph

contracts: tool_called(pre, post) — pre runs on entry; post runs on exit only when no exception was raised AND call.result has no 'error' key (success is signaled by absence of 'error', matching connector.py's existing convention across all its return shapes — there is no 'ok' key convention here, unlike taskfw).

repo_path_nudge/confidence_nudge/no_followup_nudge take plain values (repo_path str, status+confidence str, status+queries list), never a session dict or connector internals — keeps dispatcher.py decoupled from connector.py's _sessions state.

no_followup_nudge fires only on submit_report's specific 'not queries' done-branch, not the separate 'no new events from follow-up queries' done-branch — the two are different failure modes and only the former should prompt 'consider deeper SPL'.
tool-call-dispatcher.description: Self-contained pre/post hook (tool_called context manager) around connector.py's MCP-facing operations, plus three advisory nudge functions. Mirrors taskfw/dispatcher.py's pattern but for a distinct reason: not to replace a broken external-hook dependency (there wasn't one — connector.py's results were always self-sufficient), but to give the MCP tools a place to attach advisory nudges without scattering that logic inline.
invariants: apply_*_nudge functions mutate result in place, adding at most one new key (repo_path_nudge/confidence_nudge/followup_nudge) — never remove or change existing keys.
A nudge is advisory only: it never blocks a tool call or changes status/findings, only adds an optional string key the calling agent may act on.
tool-call-dispatcher.name: tool-call-dispatcher
